name: Scarlet Skips Beginner Guide
description: Start with a jump you can repeat, learn where to watch the rope and avoid the early picks that make everything harder too soon.
imageAlt: Scarlet jumping a red and white rope in the park

sections.heading: What Is Scarlet Skips?
paragraphs: Scarlet Skips is a one-button score game from Yerk Games. You press, hold and release to jump, then choose one of three random upgrades whenever you level up. That sounds simple, and for the first few skips it is.

The fun starts when the upgrades mess with the rhythm you just learned. More height changes where you land, more speed gives you less time to react, and extra ropes fill in the gaps you were using. Later on, Rocket Fuel can turn the whole run into one long flight.
bullets: It launched on Steam for Windows on September 3, 2026.
There are 10 upgrade cards, and each level-up shows 3 random choices.
It is single-player, upgrades can stack, and Steam currently lists one achievement.

sections.heading: Basic Controls
paragraphs: There is only one gameplay input: press, hold and release. Press just before the rope reaches Scarlet's feet, hold only as long as you need, then release with the next rope pass already in mind.
Scarlet's animation is easy to stare at, but the better cue is the point where the rope meets the ground. Watch that spot and the timing becomes much easier to repeat.
bullets: Let the rope make one full turn before you rush the first jump.
Start with short, repeatable presses instead of holding for maximum height.
When an upgrade changes the timing, spend a few loops learning the new beat.
Use whichever mouse, keyboard or controller binding feels easiest to repeat.

sections.heading: A First-30-Seconds Practice Routine
paragraphs: Forget the score for the first half-minute. Your only job is to make the first rope feel boring and predictable. Once you know what a normal jump looks like, every upgrade is easier to judge.
bullets: First pass: do nothing and watch where the rope crosses the ground.
Next few passes: use the same short press and notice where Scarlet lands.
Landing too close to the next pass? Release earlier instead of jumping higher.
After the first upgrade, change one thing and give yourself a few loops to adjust.

sections.heading: How Jump Timing Works
paragraphs: The best jump is not always the highest one. You only need enough room to clear the current pattern and land somewhere you can read. Jump too late and the rope catches you; hold too long and you may simply move the mistake to the landing.

Jump Height and Rocket Fuel can make a good run feel completely different from its opening. If the old timing suddenly stops working, slow down for a few loops. That does not mean the upgrade was bad.
bullets: Leave enough room to clear the rope without dropping into the next pass.
Hold longer only when the pattern really needs more airtime.
Near the top of the jump, look for the next rope instead of staring at Scarlet.
Treat a new rope or a speed increase as a new rhythm to learn.

sections.heading: How Leveling and Upgrade Choices Work
paragraphs: A level-up pauses the run and gives you three random cards from a pool of ten. You cannot force a perfect order, so work with what the game gives you instead of waiting for a checklist to line up.
Before you click, ask: what is making this run dangerous right now? Which card helps the goal I actually care about? And can I learn its new timing on the very next loop?
bullets: Pick for this run, not for an imaginary perfect build.
If the next landing already looks bad, take the card that keeps you alive.
Do not chase a combo when neither card fixes the problem in front of you.
If all three choices pull in different directions, compare them in the Build Planner.

sections.heading: Which Upgrades Should Beginners Prioritize?
paragraphs: Jump Height is the easiest early pick to feel, and Reinforce Jump Rope is useful when one break would wreck the setup. Players also like Luck early, although the developer has not published an exact formula for what it changes.
Leave rope speed, extra ropes and fire alone until the current pattern feels comfortable. Rocket Fuel is much better after a normal jump already stays up for several rope turns.
bullets: Need more breathing room? Take Jump Height, then relearn the landing.
Afraid the setup will collapse? Reinforce the rope before adding more pressure.
Everything feels safe? Luck has more of the run left to help.
Already clearing several turns? Rocket Fuel finally has somewhere useful to take you.

sections.heading: Common Beginner Mistakes
paragraphs: Most early runs go wrong because too many things change at once. When you lose, think back to the first upgrade after which the rhythm felt messy. That choice usually tells you more than the final missed rope.
bullets: Watching Scarlet instead of the rope touching the ground.
Holding every jump as long as possible.
Reacting to one rope at a time instead of watching the whole pattern.
Adding speed, another rope and fire before the new beat feels comfortable.
Copying a high-score route when you are still trying to survive.

sections.heading: First Build Recommendation
paragraphs: Keep the rope set small, protect it, and take enough height that your landings stop feeling tight. After that, add Luck or Rocket Fuel one card at a time. From there you can turn the run toward the ending, a bigger score or just more practice.
bullets: Keep the first plan boring on purpose.
Add one timing change at a time.
Decide whether you want the ending or a score before the late run gets busy.

sections.heading: When Should You Add More Ropes?
paragraphs: Add another rope only after the current set is protected and one jump can clear several turns. High-score players often wait until the airtime setup is already producing upgrades quickly.
Once the new rope appears, watch a full pattern before you panic-jump. There is usually one repeatable gap where a single jump clears several passes. That gap is what you are looking for.
bullets: An extra rope changes the pattern; it is not free score.
The more ropes you keep, the more reinforcement matters.
Try to clear a group of passes with one long jump.
If you are chasing the ending, fewer ropes may actually be better.

sections.heading: Know When the Run Has Changed Shape
paragraphs: At some point a good run stops feeling like normal jump rope. One jump clears lots of turns, upgrades pop while Scarlet is still in the air, and Rocket Fuel carries you from one choice to the next. When that happens, watch the fuel gauge more than the landing spot.
If the run never gets there, it was not wasted. Keep the pattern readable, practice the same input and use it to learn what your next run needs.
bullets: Early run: plan each landing.
Growing run: count how many turns one jump clears and keep the ropes protected.
Airtime run: watch the fuel gauge and how long it takes to reach the next upgrade.
Score run: add speed, more ropes or fire only after the loop works more than once.

name: How to Play Scarlet Skips
description: A plain-English guide to the one button, the upgrade screen, scoring and the moment a normal jump turns into a long flight.
imageAlt: Scarlet clearing a standard rope in an official Scarlet Skips screenshot

sections.heading: Controls
paragraphs: Scarlet Skips uses one gameplay input. Steam describes the mechanic as press, hold and release; official feature tags include keyboard-only, mouse-only and partial controller support. Confirm the actual binding you want in Settings rather than assuming a guide's key list matches your setup.
bullets: Press to begin the jump input.
Hold to extend the action and, later, powered airtime.
Release to finish the input and control the landing.
The same simple input gains different consequences as upgrades stack.

sections.heading: PC Version and Requirements
paragraphs: Scarlet Skips is sold for Windows through Steam with an English interface. Price and review totals are live regional data, so use the store page for the current amount instead of treating an old search result as permanent.
bullets: Minimum: Windows 10, Intel i7-6700HQ, 8 GB RAM, GTX 1060, DirectX 12 and 2 GB storage.
Recommended: Ryzen 9 3900X, 16 GB RAM, RTX 2080, DirectX 12 and 2 GB storage.
Steam lists single-player, Steam Achievements and Family Sharing.
Developer and publisher: Yerk Games.

sections.heading: Press, Hold and Release
paragraphs: Think in one smooth cycle rather than three unrelated commands. The rope position tells you when to begin; the pattern tells you how long to hold; the next ground crossing tells you when a predictable landing matters more than extra height.
A short press is the baseline. A long hold is a tool for clearing grouped passes or spending Rocket Fuel—not the default answer to every rope.
bullets: Start with consistent short cycles.
Use longer holds only after height or Rocket Fuel changes the run.
Release early enough to observe and plan the descent.
Avoid automatic tapping once several ropes are active.

sections.heading: Jump Timing
paragraphs: The strongest visual reference is the rope crossing the ground near Scarlet's feet. Begin shortly before contact, clear the pass, and shift attention toward the next rotation before the apex.
With multiple ropes, do not react to each strand as a separate event. Watch a complete rotation, identify the largest repeating gap and use one jump to clear a group of passes when height allows.
bullets: Higher is not always safer if it produces a blind landing.
Speed compresses the reaction window.
Extra ropes create a pattern of safe and unsafe gaps.
After any rhythm-changing pick, use several low-risk cycles to recalibrate.

sections.heading: Level Ups
paragraphs: Continuing to skip advances the run until play pauses for an upgrade choice. The official store confirms ten cards in total and three random choices at each level-up.
Repeated cards matter because upgrades stack. The useful question is not only which card is strongest, but which stack makes the current run safer or moves it toward a specific goal.
bullets: The game pauses for the decision.
The same card can reappear because upgrades stack.
Random offers make flexible plans stronger than fixed scripts.
Community routes report that later aerial builds can receive more than one upgrade during a jump.

sections.heading: Upgrade Choices
paragraphs: Choose for the run you have. Height and protection stabilize; Luck and fuel support progression and airtime; quantity, speed and fire add late pressure. Exact values have not been officially published.

Before clicking, classify the offer: immediate survival, progression, airtime or score. If the run is already unstable, an indirect synergy can be weaker than a plain card that preserves the next cycle.
bullets: Check the current weakness before chasing a synergy.
Change one timing variable at a time when possible.
Do not treat community priorities as guaranteed optimums.
Version 1.0.1 specifically fixed Rocket Shoes and extinguished-rope behavior.

sections.heading: Scoring and Progression
paragraphs: Successful rope loops raise the visible counter. Additional ropes, speed, long airtime and fire can change how quickly a developed run grows, but Yerk Games has not published a complete score or level-up formula.
One community route reached roughly 200,000 and another player's footage reaches the ending; neither result defines an official leaderboard or required threshold.
bullets: Survival keeps the counter and upgrade engine moving.
Fire adds a visible multiplier state in official screenshots.
A reported high-score route delays fire until height, Luck and fuel are stable.
No official global leaderboard is currently documented.

sections.heading: The Airtime Transition
paragraphs: A developed run can stop behaving like ordinary jump rope. Community guides report that high Jump Height, fast progression and Rocket Fuel may produce several level-ups in one jump; one guide also reports that each upgrade refreshes fuel.
Treat this as a testable player-discovered loop. Watch the gauge, confirm the refill on the current patch and preserve a safe landing until the sequence repeats.
bullets: Height creates more rotations per jump.
Progression must arrive before fuel expires.
Fuel bridges one upgrade to the next.
Late rope count, speed and fire convert the stable engine into score pressure.

sections.heading: Losing and Recovering
paragraphs: A missed rope ends the attempt. Diagnose backward from the miss: did launch timing drift, did a longer hold create a bad landing, or did the last upgrade add a pattern you never stopped to read?
Use the next run to change one decision at a time. The first destabilizing choice usually teaches more than the final input.
bullets: Identify the first decision that changed the rhythm.
Practice the new timing before adding another variable.
Keep a smaller protected rope set if visual tracking is the blocker.
Log the next run level by level in the Build Planner.

sections.heading: Win and Ending Basics
paragraphs: Community evidence and long-form gameplay confirm that Scarlet Skips has an ending. A documented route uses early progression, simplifies and reinforces the rope set, then stacks height, Luck and fuel while avoiding fire.
The final sequence begins around the Super Rocket Shoes state. The dedicated Ending Guide keeps the visual outcome hidden until you choose to reveal it.
bullets: The ending route is separate from a pure high-score route.
A smaller reinforced rope set is part of the documented approach.
No official numeric height requirement has been published.
Use the spoiler-controlled Ending Guide for the full route.

sections.heading: What Is Confirmed and What Is Not
paragraphs: Official facts cover the one-button loop, ten-card pool, three choices per level, stackable upgrades, release details and a few example effects. Exact card formulas, caps and optimal routes remain undocumented.
This site keeps player observations useful by labeling them. A reproduced result is stronger than a guess, but it is still not a developer guarantee.
bullets: Official: store copy, API fields, patch notes and visible official media.
Community Verified: corroborated behavior or clearly visible repeated play.
Player Report: one route, threshold or interaction that still needs broader testing.
Unconfirmed: rumor or inference that should not be used as a rule.

name: Scarlet Skips Tips & Tricks
description: Practical fixes for shaky openings, awkward landings, rope overload and the Rocket Fuel loop that players use for long runs.
imageAlt: Scarlet reacting as rope segments break during a difficult run

sections.heading: Early Run: Protect Information
paragraphs: Use the opening to establish a repeatable beat. A run is easier to diagnose when early upgrades change one variable at a time; a score burst is less useful than knowing exactly why the next jump succeeds.
bullets: Prefer readable height or protection picks.
Delay fire and heavy rope pressure.
Take Luck only when the current landing is safe.
Watch a full rotation after every pattern-changing choice.

sections.heading: Jump Timing: Plan the Descent
paragraphs: Read the rope against the ground and plan the landing, not only the launch. A jump can clear the incoming pass and still fail because the hold placed Scarlet into the next rotation.
bullets: Short consistent jumps teach more than maximum holds.
Shift attention to the next pass near the apex.
After a height stack, reset your internal beat.
Use Rocket Fuel as a controlled extension, not a panic button.

sections.heading: Upgrade Decisions: Ask Four Questions
paragraphs: The best card is goal-dependent. On the paused choice screen, classify the run before comparing names.
bullets: What ends the run now: clearance, landing, rope loss or slow progression?
Which offer directly fixes that problem?
Which card advances the chosen ending, score or airtime goal?
Which change can you observe and relearn on the next cycle?

sections.heading: Rope Management
paragraphs: Every additional rope increases what you must read and maintain. Quantity becomes an advantage only when one jump can clear grouped passes and the build can protect or replace losses.
bullets: Reinforce a small set before scaling it.
Read the complete spacing pattern instead of the nearest rope.
Let excess ropes go if an ending route needs more control.
Add quantity late in community high-score routes.

sections.heading: Airtime and the Refill Test
paragraphs: Height creates the opportunity; Rocket Fuel extends it; progression must arrive before the gauge empties if you want the reported loop.
One high-score author reports that an upgrade refills fuel. Verify that behavior in the current run, then require it to succeed twice before abandoning a safe landing plan.
bullets: Stack the height and progression foundation first.
Watch the gauge at the exact moment a level-up resolves.
Keep a recoverable landing until the loop repeats.
Expect later level-ups to take longer and budget more fuel margin.

sections.heading: Luck Without an Invented Formula
paragraphs: Players strongly prioritize Increase Luck, and a separate Spanish guide also describes it as affecting perk quality or availability. Yerk Games has not published a formula, so judge Luck through actual run feedback rather than a claimed percentage.
bullets: Early value has more time to compound.
Look for changes in Lucky feedback and upgrade cadence.
A reported cap is not a confirmed cap.
Direct survival still outranks an indirect benefit when the run is unstable.

sections.heading: High Score Transition
paragraphs: Build the engine before the multiplier. One published route stayed near two to four ropes early and used roughly twelve loops per jump as a personal transition point before scaling harder.
That number is not a requirement. The real signal is functional: several upgrades arrive during an extended jump and fuel still remains for the next bridge.
bullets: Height and Luck first.
Fuel loop second.
Rope speed and quantity after the loop is repeatable.
Fire last, when rope losses are sustainable.

sections.heading: Ending Transition
paragraphs: The cited winning route uses the opposite late priorities from a score build. It grows progression early, allows surplus ropes to disappear, reinforces the controlled set, then stacks height, Luck and fuel while avoiding fire.
bullets: Do not preserve every rope out of sunk-cost thinking.
Reinforce before the long height push.
Treat the reported 50,000 height as one run's snapshot, not a requirement.
Super Rocket Shoes is the reported final-ascent signal.

sections.heading: Diagnose a Failed Run
paragraphs: Runs often fail because several upgrades change the same timing window at once. Work backward from the miss and record the first point at which the pattern became unreadable.
bullets: Late launch: recalibrate against the ground crossing.
Unsafe landing: shorten the hold or save fuel for descent control.
Rope overload: stop adding quantity and reinforce or simplify.
Slow upgrade cadence: invest in progression before more fuel.
Fire collapse: return to a protected non-fire engine.

sections.heading: Claims to Treat Carefully
paragraphs: Launch-week guides are valuable but young. The roughly 200,000 run, suspected Luck and speed caps, fuel refills and specific transition counts are player observations rather than developer documentation.
bullets: Do not call a reported score a world record.
Do not publish a cap without a repeatable test and version.
Do not turn one successful route into a mandatory card order.
Recheck any behavior after patches mentioning Rocket Shoes or extinguished ropes.

name: Scarlet Skips Achievement Guide
description: Want the only Steam achievement? Here is the very short answer, plus what to try if it does not unlock.
imageAlt: Off to a Great Start achievement icon from Scarlet Skips

sections.heading: Achievement Facts
paragraphs: Steam lists one achievement for Scarlet Skips: Off to a Great Start. The official data confirms the count and name, while the trigger is documented by players rather than explained on the public store page.
bullets: Total Steam achievements: 1.
Name: Off to a Great Start.
Steam category: Steam Achievements.
Public official requirement text: not documented in the store data checked.

sections.heading: Before You Start
paragraphs: The achievement is tied to the opening failure, so the cleanest attempt is a fresh launch or fresh first run. One guide notes that the opening sequence can be advanced with the same held input; release it before gameplay begins so Scarlet does not jump accidentally.
bullets: Launch Scarlet Skips through Steam while online.
Advance or watch the intro.
Release every jump-capable input before the first rope reaches Scarlet.
Do not perform a successful skip first.

sections.heading: How to Unlock Off to a Great Start
paragraphs: Two independent Steam Community guides describe the same trigger: fail the first jump. When the first active rope arrives, do nothing and let it catch Scarlet.
bullets: Start a new run.
Keep mouse, keyboard and controller jump inputs untouched.
Let the first rope hit Scarlet's feet.
Wait for the Steam achievement notification before starting another attempt.

sections.heading: Why This Is Community Verified
paragraphs: The method is stronger than a single anecdote because two separate Steam guides document the same first-failure trigger. It is still labeled Community Verified rather than Official because Yerk Games has not published the requirement in the checked store data.
bullets: Official evidence confirms the achievement exists.
Two community sources agree on the trigger.
The method is simple enough to reproduce in a new run.
Future patches could still change the behavior or add achievements.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: If it does not unlock, remove ambiguity before assuming the method is wrong. Restart the game, confirm Steam is online and make a clean attempt without any keyboard, mouse or controller input after the run becomes active.
bullets: Check that Steam is online and achievement notifications are enabled.
Disconnect or release a controller with a stuck or drifting input.
Do not hold the intro-skip input into the first active rope cycle.
Restart and try a fresh first miss before completing a successful skip.
Recheck the current game version and linked guides after a future patch.
